summary_paragraph: A man with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic heart failure, diabetes, and Chagas disease was admitted for monitoring due to a six-day history of influenza-like illness including fever, productive cough, sore throat, and myalgias. He was started empirically on Tamiflu given his comorbidities, but the influenza test returned negative, so antiviral therapy was discontinued. Supportive care with cough suppressants and acetaminophen was provided. His symptoms improved during the 24-hour stay, and blood cultures showed no growth. He remained euvolemic with stable vital signs and was discharged home with instructions to continue his regular medications, manage symptoms, and attend scheduled dialysis. Follow-up was advised with primary care and cardiology.
problems: Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
Chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
